title.rendered: Speak to the Mountain | Teach Me How to Pray, Day 6

excerpt.rendered: On the road from Bethany to Jerusalem, Jesus gave His disciples the clearest teaching on declarative prayer in the New Testament. He did not tell them to beg. He told them to speak to the mountain.

content.rendered:
On the road from Bethany to Jerusalem, between a cursed fig tree and the Temple cleansing, Jesus gave His disciples the clearest teaching on authoritative, declarative prayer in the entire New Testament. He did not tell them to beg God to move the mountain. He told them to speak to it.

The Gospel For Today | Thursday, October 8, 2026 | Teach Me How to Pray, Day 6

Today’s Scripture

“So Jesus answered and said to them, ‘Have faith in God. For assuredly, I say to you, whoever says to this mountain, Be removed and be cast into the sea, and does not doubt in his heart, but believes that those things he says will be done, he will have whatever he says. Therefore I say to you, whatever things you ask when you pray, believe that you receive them, and you will have them.'”
Mark 11:22-24 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

It was the week of Passover. Jesus and His disciples were walking the road from Bethany, where they had been staying with Lazarus, up to Jerusalem for the day’s teaching in the Temple. The previous morning, Jesus had cursed a fig tree that had leaves but no fruit. By the next morning, as they passed the same tree on the way back, Peter noticed something that stopped him in his tracks. “Rabbi, look! The fig tree which You cursed has withered away.” The entire tree, from root to crown, was dead. In less than twenty-four hours. Jesus had spoken to it once. The tree had died in response. And in that moment, Jesus gave His disciples the clearest teaching on declarative, authority-based prayer in the entire New Testament.

“Have faith in God. For assuredly, I say to you, whoever says to this mountain, Be removed and be cast into the sea, and does not doubt in his heart, but believes that those things he says will be done, he will have whatever he says.” Notice the verbs Jesus uses. The believer does not ask God to move the mountain. The believer says to the mountain. The believer speaks to the mountain. And the mountain, Jesus promises, obeys the words of a believer who does not doubt but believes. This is not a parable. It is not a metaphor Jesus is being cute with. The mountain is any obstacle, any opposition, any immovable circumstance in the believer’s life. And the authority to command it to move is in the believer’s words, spoken in faith, from a heart rooted in Christ.

The Passion Translation renders this passage with striking force: “Jesus replied, ‘Let the faith of God be in you! Listen to the truth I speak to you: Whoever says to this mountain with great faith and does not doubt, Mountain, be lifted up and thrown into the midst of the sea, and believes that what he says will happen, it will be done. This is the reason I urge you to boldly believe for whatever you ask for in prayer—believe that you have received it and it will be yours'” (Mark 11:22-24 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds a critical phrase: “Jesus, replying, said to them, Have faith in God [constantly]… For truly I tell you, whoever says to this mountain, Be lifted up and thrown into the sea! and does not doubt at all in his heart but believes that what he says will take place, it will be done for him” (Mark 11:22-23 AMPC). “It will be done for him.” That is a promise from the lips of Jesus Himself.

How Jesus Prayed

The Format. Jesus taught two directions of spiritual communication. Upward — ask the Father, believe you receive. Outward — speak to the mountain, command the circumstance. Most believers only pray upward. Jesus taught both. The authority He gave the believer flows in both directions.

The Essence. This is the core of New Testament prayer. The believer does not merely request. The believer declares, in faith, from the authority of Christ, over the circumstances of life. The mountain is not consulted. The mountain is commanded. And the mountain, Jesus promised, will move.

The Authority. The authority of the believer’s words is the authority of the Christ who indwells them. The believer who speaks to a mountain in Jesus’ name is not speaking in the believer’s own strength or wisdom. The believer is extending the authority of the risen Christ into the earth. The mountain hears the voice of Jesus coming through the mouth of the believer. And the mountain obeys.

The Assurance. “He will have whatever he says.” The condition is faith without doubt, grounded in the finished work of Christ. The assurance is total. Not maybe. Not sometimes. Not if God is in a good mood. He will have what he says. The believer’s words, spoken in faith, carry the weight of heaven’s decree.

The Submission. The teaching comes with an immediate follow-up in verse 25. “And whenever you stand praying, if you have anything against anyone, forgive him, that your Father in heaven may also forgive you your trespasses.” Authority in prayer is paired with a forgiven and forgiving heart. The believer who holds unforgiveness forfeits the authority Jesus is describing. The two must walk together.

The Result. Mountains move. Trees wither. Storms calm. Sickness leaves. Finances open. Doors swing wide. The believer who learns to speak to circumstances in the authority of Christ sees Kingdom results in the earth. For Gospelbuzz readers today, wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, what is the mountain in your life this week? Name it. Then do what Jesus taught. Speak to it. Not around it. Not about it. To it. In the name of Jesus, from a heart that does not doubt, command it to move. The mountain is listening.

Prayer (Pattern After Jesus)

Address (upward). Father, I thank You that the authority Jesus walked in has been placed on me. The same Spirit that raised Him from the dead lives in me. I live in the finished work of the cross.

Command (outward, to the mountain). In the name of Jesus, I speak to [name the mountain — the sickness, the debt, the closed door, the opposition, the crisis]. I command you to be removed and cast into the sea. You will not stand in my life. You will not stop the Father’s will in this matter. Be lifted up. Be gone.

Faith Declaration. I believe what I have said will be done. I do not doubt in my heart. I receive what the Father has promised, and the mountain is already moving.

Forgiveness Check. And where I have held anything against anyone, I release them now, so that my prayer carries the full authority Jesus intended.

In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I speak to the mountains in my life with the authority of Jesus. I do not beg the Father to move them. I command them to move in His name. What I say in faith, from a forgiven heart, is already done.
